newsitem.title: USA: REPORT SPECULATES ON CHASE-MERRILL MERGER.
newsitem.headline: REPORT SPECULATES ON CHASE-MERRILL MERGER.

text.p: Some on Wall Street speculate about a Chase Manhattan Corp and Merrill Lynch & Co merger and both have examined the possibility of a merger that would form the world's third largest banking company, sources told Business Week.
However, the report cautioned that there's no hard evidence that a deal is in the works.
A combined Chase-Merrill would have $549 billion in assets, $360 billion in assets under management and 118,000 employees, the company said.
With a market capitalization of $70 billion, a combined Chase-Merrill would be behind only Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd and Deutsche Bank AG in terms of size, the report said.

A Merrill spokesman told the magazine, "We believe we have the right strategy in place to make the most of the considerable growth opportunity ahead for Merrill Lynch and that we can, on our own, continue to do an excellent job of serving clients and building shareholder value."
"It is totally inappropriate to respond to hypothetical conjecture," a Chase spokesman told the magazine.
